cards.text: That same day, after the question about Caesar's coin (Matthew 22:15-22), the Sadducees come to Jesus with a question of their own. It's like clearing out your inbox and hearing that DING before you even sit back down. The Sadducees are a party tied to the high priest (Acts 5:17), and Matthew tells us one big thing they say.

cards.question: According to Matthew, the Sadducees who come to Jesus say there is no resurrection.

cards.text: They call Him Teacher and bring up something Moses, Israel's leader, declared. If a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow.

cards.question: In the case the Sadducees bring up from Moses, why does the brother marry his brother's widow?

answers.text: To raise up children for his brother
To pay off his brother's debts
To look after his brother's flocks

cards.text: Then they tell Jesus about seven brothers among them. The first one marries and dies without having children.

cards.question: In the Sadducees' story, the first brother dies without children. Who does he leave his wife to?

cards.text: The same thing happens to the second and third brothers, all the way down to the seventh. And last of all, the woman dies.

cards.question: Now the Sadducees ask Jesus their big question about the resurrection. What do they want to know about the woman?

answers.text: Which brother will be her husband
Which brother she loved the most
Which brother will inherit her land

cards.text: Jesus doesn't tiptoe around it. He tells them flat out they're mistaken.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Sadducees they're mistaken. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They don't know the Scriptures or God's power
They spoke without asking the priests first
They brought their question on the Sabbath

cards.text: Then Jesus answers their puzzle about the seven brothers by telling them what the resurrection is like.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Sadducees that in the resurrection, people will keep marrying just like they do now.

cards.text: Instead, Jesus says, they will be like the angels in heaven. Then He takes on the bigger question, whether the dead rise at all.

cards.question: On whether the dead rise, Jesus asks the Sadducees if they've never read something. What is it?

answers.text: What the prophets wrote about Him

cards.text: Jesus quotes God's own words: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob". Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are Israel's forefathers (Acts 3:13).

cards.question: Jesus says God is not the God of the dead, but of the ___.
When the crowds hear Jesus answer the Sadducees, they are ___ at His teaching.

cards.text: Pull this batch out of the oven, friend, but don't turn the oven off. This story's still going.
